src: Serious Eats — Daniel Gritzer — "Smooth and Creamy Polenta"

time.en: 5 min | Cook: 65 min | Total: not given

en.v: Saucier, whisk, cast iron skillet or grill (optional)

sk.v: Rajnica s guľatým dnom (saucier), metlička, liatinová panvica alebo gril (nepovinné)

c.t: Any medium or coarse cornmeal works; avoid instant polenta. Milk makes rich, creamy but heavy polenta; stock adds flavour but can mask the corn; water gives the lightest polenta with a mild corn flavour.

Poslúži akákoľvek stredne alebo hrubo mletá kukuričná krupica; nepoužívajte instantnú polentu. S mliekom bude polenta bohatá a krémová, ale ťažká; vývar pridá chuť, no môže prekryť kukuricu; voda dá najľahšiu polentu s jemnou kukuričnou chuťou.

en.t: 1180 ml water, milk, or chicken stock or vegetable stock
140 g medium or coarse cornmeal/polenta
Kosher salt
2 tbsp (30 g) unsalted butter or extra-virgin olive oil, plus more oil to sear or grill, if desired
Accompaniments, as desired

1. If Using the Presoaking Method: Combine water with cornmeal in a large mixing bowl and let stand, covered, at room temperature overnight. When ready to cook, scrape soaked cornmeal and water into a large saucier or saucepan and set over high heat. Continue with step 3.
2. If Using the Standard Method: Add water, milk, or stock to a large saucier or saucepan and set over high heat. Sprinkle in cornmeal while whisking (water does not have to be boiling).

3. Bring to a boil, stirring frequently. Let boil, stirring frequently, until polenta thickens enough that it starts to spit. Lower heat immediately to prevent spitting and continue to cook, stirring frequently with a spoon or silicone spatula and scraping bottom to prevent scorching, until polenta becomes thick and pulls away from side of saucepan, about 30 minutes for presoaked cornmeal and 50 minutes for dry cornmeal. Season with salt.

4. Stir in butter or olive oil, using either a spoon, a silicone spatula, or a whisk. Polenta will become glossy from the added fat, and should feel rich, creamy, and smooth. If polenta forms lumps, beat vigorously with a stiff whisk to remove. If polenta becomes too firm or begins to set, add a small amount of water, stock, or milk and beat in with a whisk until liquid is fully incorporated and no lumps remain.
5. Serve right away with accompaniment of your choice, or continue with step 6 to sear or grill.

6. To Sear or Grill: Grease a rimmed quarter sheet pan with olive oil. Pour hot polenta into pan, then use a spatula to spread evenly. Place a sheet of parchment or plastic wrap against surface to further smooth and even surface. Wrap pan well in plastic, and refrigerate until completely chilled and set, at least 5 hours or up to overnight.
7. Using a thin spatula, loosen block of polenta. Invert onto a cutting board. Cut polenta into squares, rectangles, triangles, or circles, as you desire.

8. To sear, heat a large cast iron skillet over high heat. Coat bottom of skillet with oil, then, when shimmering, add polenta. Cook undisturbed until browned, crisp, and easily releases from skillet, about 3 minutes. Flip and repeat on second side. To grill, heat charcoal or gas grill over high heat. Clean and oil grates. Add polenta and cook undisturbed until browned, crisp, and easily releases from grill, about 3 minutes. Flip and repeat on second side.
9. Serve topped with accompaniments of your choice (such as gorgonzola dolce).

1. Metóda s namáčaním: vo veľkej mise zmiešame vodu s kukuričnou krupicou a necháme prikryté pri izbovej teplote cez noc. Pred varením namočenú krupicu aj s vodou vyškrabeme do veľkého kastróla (saucier) a postavíme na silný oheň. Pokračujeme krokom 3.
2. Bežná metóda: do veľkého kastróla nalejeme vodu, mlieko alebo vývar a postavíme na silný oheň. Za stáleho šľahania metličkou prisypávame kukuričnú krupicu (voda nemusí vrieť).

3. Za častého miešania privedieme do varu. Varíme za častého miešania, kým polenta nezhustne natoľko, že začne prskať. Hneď stlmíme oheň, aby neprskala, a varíme ďalej za častého miešania lyžicou alebo silikónovou stierkou, pričom zoškrabujeme dno, aby sa nepripálila, kým polenta nie je hustá a neodstupuje od stien kastróla, asi 30 minút pri namočenej krupici a 50 minút pri suchej. Osolíme.

4. Lyžicou, silikónovou stierkou alebo metličkou vmiešame maslo alebo olivový olej. Polenta sa od tuku zaleskne a má byť sýta, krémová a hladká. Ak sa v nej vytvoria hrudky, energicky ju vyšľaháme pevnou metličkou. Ak polenta príliš zhustne alebo začne tuhnúť, pridáme trochu vody, vývaru alebo mlieka a metličkou vyšľaháme, kým sa tekutina úplne nezapracuje a nezostanú hrudky.
5. Podávame hneď s prílohou podľa chuti, alebo pokračujeme krokom 6 a polentu opečieme či ugrilujeme.

6. Opekanie alebo grilovanie: malý plech s okrajom (štvrtinový) vymastíme olivovým olejom. Horúcu polentu vylejeme na plech a stierkou ju rovnomerne rozotrieme. Na povrch priložíme papier na pečenie alebo fóliu, aby sa ešte viac uhladil a vyrovnal. Plech dobre zabalíme do fólie a necháme v chladničke, kým polenta úplne nevychladne a nestuhne, aspoň 5 hodín alebo cez noc.
7. Tenkou obracačkou blok polenty uvoľníme. Vyklopíme ho na dosku. Polentu nakrájame na štvorce, obdĺžniky, trojuholníky alebo kruhy podľa chuti.

8. Opekanie: veľkú liatinovú panvicu rozpálime na silnom ohni. Dno potrieme olejom, a keď sa olej zaleskne, pridáme polentu. Opekáme bez manipulácie, kým nie je zhnednutá, chrumkavá a ľahko sa neodlepí od panvice, asi 3 minúty. Obrátime a rovnako opečieme druhú stranu. Grilovanie: gril na drevené uhlie alebo plynový gril rozpálime na vysokú teplotu. Rošt očistíme a naolejujeme. Pridáme polentu a grilujeme bez manipulácie, kým nie je zhnednutá, chrumkavá a ľahko sa neodlepí od roštu, asi 3 minúty. Obrátime a rovnako ugrilujeme druhú stranu.
9. Podávame s prílohou podľa chuti (napríklad s jemnou gorgonzolou dolce).

src: Serious Eats — Nargisse Benkabbou — "Simple Fluffy Couscous"

time.en: 15 min | Cook: 30 min | Total: 45 min

c.t: Buy couscous made from 100% durum wheat semolina.
Kupujte kuskus zo 100 % semoliny z tvrdej pšenice.

en.t: 510 g dry couscous
360 g cold or room temperature homemade chicken or vegetable stock or store bought low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth or water, plus more as needed
1/2 tsp (1.5 g) kosher salt; for table salt or fine sea salt use half by volume, plus more to taste
3 tbsp (45 ml) olive oil or melted butter

1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C). In a 23 × 33 cm baking dish, add couscous and pour the liquid over top. Use your hands to mix the couscous evenly, making sure all the grains are moistened. Let sit at room temperature until all liquid is absorbed, about 15 minutes.

2. Use your fingers (or a fork) to separate the grains of couscous until light, fluffy, and well separated. Check their consistency—the grains should be plump but still hold their shape when pressed between two fingers. If your couscous is still hard, add 120 ml of stock, broth, or water, let sit for 15 additional minutes, and fluff again.
3. Add salt and olive oil or melted butter to grains and use fingers to mix thoroughly.
4. Cover tightly with foil and bake until couscous grains are fully tender and hot, 30 to 35 minutes. Fluff with a fork and season to taste with salt. Serve.

1. Toast quinoa in medium saucepan over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until quinoa is very fragrant and makes continuous popping sound, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer quinoa to bowl and set aside.
2. Return now-empty pan to medium-low heat and melt butter. Add onion and salt; cook, stirring frequently, until onion is softened and light golden, 5 to 7 minutes.

3. Increase heat to medium-high, stir in water and quinoa, and bring to simmer. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until grains are just tender and liquid is absorbed, 18 to 20 minutes, stirring once halfway through cooking. 1. In a medium bowl, cover black-eyed peas with 5 cm water. Let soak at room temperature for at least 15 minutes and up to 1 hour (this short soaking time helps loosen the skins without overly softening the peas).

2. Drain peas then transfer to a countertop blender or food processor along with 945 ml water. Pulse to slightly break up peas, about ten 1-second pulses. Pour into a medium bowl and let stand at room temperature for up to 30 minutes (skins will float to top as they separate from the peas).

3. Set a colander over a large bowl. Slowly pour soaking water into the colander while using a free hand to keep the peas in the soaking bowl; the goal is to pour off as much of the floating skins as possible while leaving the peas behind. Pick out any peas that landed in the colander and return them to the bowl, then discard skins and soaking water. Cover peas with water, and repeat process until peas are nearly free of skins (you may need to gently massage the peas with your hands to separate any stubborn skins).
4. Transfer skinned peas to the bowl. Add 475 ml water and let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes (this will further soften the peas for blending).

5. Drain peas then transfer to a countertop blender or food processor. Add onion, bell pepper, stock, salt, and habanero or Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Blend, scraping down sides occasionally with a flexible spatula, until a smooth purée has formed, about 3 to 4 minutes (if you rub the purée between your fingers, you shouldn’t see any recognizable pea chunks). Transfer purée to a large bowl, add oil, and whisk until well combined.

6. To Make Moin Moin in Leaves: Using a sharp knife, trim stalks from bottom of moin moin leaves. Arrange stalks in an even layer at the bottom of a large pot. Alternatively, skip the stalks and place a steaming rack instead. Cover with 2 leaves, to form a bed for steaming. Fill pot with 1.5 cm of hot water, or just to the top of the rack and set aside.

7. In one hand, hold a moin moin leaf vertically with the shiny side up. Set a second leaf on top of the first so that the base of their midribs meet and the second leaf is angled a little less than 45° from the first leaf (it should look like the leaves are the hands of a clock, joined at their base with the first leaf pointing to 12 o'clock and the second leaf pointing to just past 1 o'clock).

8. Using both hands and starting from the first leaf, roll the leaves to form a cone with the base of the midribs at the bottom point and open at the top. Fold the bottom 5 cm of the cone back and up to seal the base.

9. Holding the cone with its open top facing up (and securing the folded bottom with one hand), spoon (115 g) moin moin purée into cone. Set an egg quarter in the center of the purée, then cover with 58 g purée.

10. To close the cone, use your fingers to push a section at the top of the leaf cone in so it lays flat against the surface of the purée, then fold a second adjacent leaf section in over the first one. Fold the remaining excess leaf back and down so it meets the folded-up point at the base (they may not touch, or they may overlap, depending on the size of the leaves). Set the sealed leaf cone down on the bed of stems in the pot with the tucked-in ends on the underside to hold them in place (you may need to stack the cones on top of one another). Repeat with remaining leaves and purée; you should have 7 filled moin moin.

11. Place 2 or 3 additional moin moin leaves on top of the cones, cover the pot, and bring to a boil over high heat. 3. Set a colander over a large bowl. Slowly pour soaking water into the colander while using a free hand to keep the peas in the soaking bowl; the goal is to pour off as much of the floating skins as possible while leaving the peas behind. Pick out any peas that landed in the colander and return them to the bowl, then discard skins and soaking water. Cover peas with water, and repeat process until peas are nearly free of skins (you may need to gently massage the peas with your hands to separate any stubborn skins).

To close the cone, use your fingers to push a section at the top of the leaf cone in so it lays flat against the surface of the purée, then fold a second adjacent leaf section in over the first one. Fold the remaining excess leaf back and down so it meets the folded-up point at the base (they may not touch, or they may overlap, depending on the size of the leaves). Set the sealed leaf cone down on the bed of stems in the pot with the tucked-in ends on the underside to hold them in place (you may need to stack the cones on top of one another). Be sure to check water level occasionally, topping up with more boiling water from the sides as needed to keep the pot from going dry. Transfer ramekins to a wire rack and let cool for 10 minutes to allow the moin moin to firm up.

1. V strednej mise zalejeme fazuľu čiernooké oko vodou tak, aby bola 5 cm pod hladinou. Necháme namáčať pri izbovej teplote aspoň 15 minút a najviac 1 hodinu (krátke namáčanie uvoľní šupky, no fazuľa príliš nezmäkne).

2. Fazuľu scedíme a preložíme do stolového mixéra alebo kuchynského robota spolu s 945 ml vody. Pulzne ju trochu rozdrvíme, asi desaťkrát po 1 sekunde. Vylejeme do strednej misy a necháme postáť pri izbovej teplote najviac 30 minút (šupky sa pri oddeľovaní vyplavia na povrch).

3. Na veľkú misu postavíme cedidlo. Pomaly do neho slievame vodu, pričom voľnou rukou zadržiavame fazuľu v mise; cieľom je zliať čo najviac plávajúcich šupiek a fazuľu nechať v mise. Zrnká, ktoré skončili v cedidle, vyberieme a vrátime do misy, šupky aj vodu vyhodíme. Fazuľu znova zalejeme vodou a postup opakujeme, kým nie je takmer bez šupiek (tvrdohlavé šupky môžeme oddeliť jemným masírovaním rukami).
4. Ošúpanú fazuľu preložíme do misy. Pridáme 475 ml vody a necháme 10 minút postáť pri izbovej teplote (fazuľa ešte zmäkne a lepšie sa rozmixuje).

5. Fazuľu scedíme a preložíme do stolového mixéra alebo kuchynského robota. Pridáme cibuľu, papriku, vývar, soľ a papričku habanero alebo Scotch bonnet (ak ju používame). Mixujeme dohladka, asi 3 až 4 minúty; občas zotrieme steny ohybnou stierkou (po rozotretí medzi prstami by nemali byť cítiť kúsky fazule). Pyré preložíme do veľkej misy, pridáme olej a metličkou dobre premiešame.

6. Moin moin v listoch: ostrým nožom odrežeme stopky z listov moin moin. Stopky rovnomerne rozložíme na dno veľkého hrnca. Prípadne stopky vynecháme a vložíme mriežku na varenie v pare. Prikryjeme 2 listami, aby vzniklo lôžko na varenie v pare. Do hrnca nalejeme horúcu vodu do výšky 1,5 cm alebo práve po vrch mriežky a odložíme.

7. V jednej ruke držíme list moin moin zvisle lesklou stranou nahor. Druhý list položíme na prvý tak, aby sa spodky ich hlavných žiliek stretli a druhý list bol od prvého odklonený o niečo menej ako 45° (listy majú vyzerať ako ručičky hodín spojené pri spodku: prvý list ukazuje na 12 a druhý tesne za 1).
8. Oboma rukami listy od prvého listu zrolujeme do kornútu so spodkami žiliek v spodnej špičke a otvoreným vrchom. Spodných 5 cm kornútu preložíme dozadu a nahor, aby sa spodok uzavrel.
9. Kornút držíme otvorom nahor (preložený spodok pridržiavame jednou rukou) a lyžicou doň dáme 115 g pyré moin moin. Do stredu pyré vložíme štvrtinu vajca a prikryjeme ju 58 g pyré.

10. Zatváranie kornútu: prstami zatlačíme časť vrchu kornútu dovnútra, aby ležala naplocho na povrchu pyré, a cez ňu preložíme susednú časť listu. Zvyšok listu preložíme dozadu a nadol k preloženej špičke pri spodku (podľa veľkosti listov sa nemusia dotýkať alebo sa môžu prekrývať). Uzavretý kornút položíme na lôžko zo stopiek v hrnci zastrčenými koncami nadol, aby držali (kornúty môžeme ukladať na seba). Rovnako spracujeme zvyšné listy a pyré; mali by sme mať 7 plnených moin moin.

11. Na kornúty položíme ďalšie 2 až 3 listy moin moin, hrniec prikryjeme a na silnom ohni privedieme do varu. Oheň stlmíme na stredný a varíme v pare, kým listy nezmenia farbu zo sviežej na matnú zelenú a moin moin nevonia, asi 40 minút. Prípadne skúšobná špajdľa zapichnutá do najhrubšej časti má vyjsť suchá. Každých 10 až 15 minút skontrolujeme hladinu vody a podľa potreby dolejeme vriacu vodu pri stenách hrnca, aby nevyschol. Uvarené moin moin preložíme na mriežku a necháme 10 minút chladnúť, aby stuhli.

12. Moin moin v zapekacích miskách: vnútro 7 zapekacích misiek s objemom 120 ml zľahka vymastíme olejom. Lyžicou naplníme misky pyré do polovice. Do stredu každej misky vložíme štvrtinu vajca reznou stranou nahor a prikryjeme zvyšným pyré, kým nie sú misky asi do troch štvrtín plné (pyré pri varení nabehne).

13. Do veľkého hrnca nalejeme vodu do výšky 10 cm. Vložíme mriežku na varenie v pare, postavíme na ňu naplnené misky, prikryjeme a na silnom ohni privedieme do varu. Oheň stlmíme na stredný a varíme, kým moin moin nevytvoria navrchu kupolky, nie sú na dotyk pevné a po zatlačení sa nevracajú späť, asi 30 minút. Občas skontrolujeme hladinu vody a podľa potreby dolejeme vriacu vodu pri stenách hrnca, aby nevyschol. Misky preložíme na mriežku a necháme 10 minút chladnúť, aby moin moin stuhli.

14. Podávame v listoch alebo v miskách; ak chceme moin moin z misiek vyklopiť, prejdeme nožom na maslo po okrajoch, na misku položíme servírovací tanier a obrátime. Podávame samostatne, so šalátom, namočeným garri alebo sladenou ovsenou kašou, prípadne k ryži jollof alebo nigérijskej vyprážanej ryži.

1. For the Onions: In a large stainless steel sauté pan, heat 4 tbsp (60 ml) olive oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add onions and cook, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes and scraping the bottom with a wooden spoon as needed, until they have softened, collapsed significantly in volume, and are just beginning to turn golden, about 12 minutes (pan will appear very overcrowded at the beginning).

2. Reduce heat to medium and continue cooking, stirring and scraping bottom of pan every 1 to 2 minutes, until onions are fully softened and lightly golden, about 8 minutes. Off heat, transfer about 150 g onions to a small bowl and set aside.

3. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp (1.5 g) kosher salt over the remaining onions in pan and return to medium heat. Cook, stirring and scraping bottom of pan every 1 to 2 minutes, until onions are deep golden brown, about 10 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low, and continue cooking, stirring and scraping bottom of pan every 2 minutes, until deeply caramelized with some darker edges and a few lightly crisped bits, about 10 minutes (some onions may brown more deeply than others; this is expected and adds welcome flavor and texture to the final dish). Set aside.

4. For the Lentils and Rice: While onions caramelize, in a large pot, add lentils, 720 ml water, and 1 tsp (5 ml) kosher salt. Bring lentil mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Opekáme dozlatista a občas obraciame, asi 3 minúty. Tofu preložíme na tanier vystlaný papierovými utierkami, aby odkvaplo.

2. Wok vrátime na silný oheň a pridáme huby. Opekáme za občasného miešania a prehadzovania, kým huby nepustia šťavu a nezačnú hnednúť, asi 4 minúty. Pridáme cesnak a čili papričky a za stáleho miešania opekáme, kým nezavoňajú, asi 15 sekúnd. Pridáme fermentované čierne bôby a restujeme, kým sa neprehrejú, asi 30 sekúnd. Pridáme vývar a sójovú omáčku.

3. Keď zmes začne mierne vrieť, oheň stlmíme na stredný, pridáme špenát a varíme, kým nezvädne, asi 15 sekúnd. Vrátime tofu do woku a podľa potreby dosolíme. Vmiešame zmes kukuričného škrobu s vodou a varíme, kým tekutina nezhustne. Pridáme jarnú cibuľku, dobre premiešame a odstavíme z ohňa. Pridáme čili olej. Podávame ihneď s ryžou.
